Short summary of what I see from our side after 30m of digging:
- No deploys or config rollouts during the window. No infra CPU/GPU saturation on their serving cluster.
- We did observe a sustained ~3x increase in inbound request rate for their account between 20:40-21:30 UTC on 11/17. The majority of extra arrivals bear identical payloads and similar idempotency headers.
- Server traces show a classic "retry storm" pattern: many short-lived client timeouts followed by immediate retries that push requests into queueing/backpressure and cause high tail latency (p95/p99).
- Concurrently our worker queue depth for that customer spiked, increasing tokenization and KV cache pressure; p50 stayed fine while p95/p99 regressed.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be actioned immediately):
1) Apply per-account soft throttling (token-bucket) to dampen retry bursts — reduces queueing.
2) Turn on a temporary per-route circuit-breaker after sustained 429/5xx rates to protect other tenants.
3) Ask the customer to update to SDK v2.1.4 (contains improved backoff + jitter) and increase client timeout from 250ms to 2s for long-running requests.

Longer term: we need better server-side ingress-level correlation (idempotency key tracking) and a tracing sample that correlates client retry attempts to server arrival times to prove causality.

I'll prepare a short timeline + logs to share with the customer. Attaching server-side sample logs.

Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Jesse —

Thanks for the traces. Quick update from our side after correlating your spans with server logs: we see a tight loop of client timeouts configured at ~250ms, followed by immediate retries with no jitter. Those retries line up with the exact spike window you reported. The retries increased sustained load and led to queueing at our ingress, which in turn increased your observed p95/p99 and 5xxs.

What we need you to try now (low-touch):
- Temporarily set client socket/read timeout to 2s for the affected calls.
- Upgrade to SDK v2.1.4 (we've attached the patch) which adds exponential backoff + jitter by default.
- If possible, enable idempotency keys on the request level to avoid duplicate processing.

We realize this looked like an API regression; from the traces it appears client retry behavior is the proximate cause. We'll also take server-side protective steps (soft throttling + circuit-breaker) while you roll this out.

Hannah will coordinate a live debug session if you'd like — we can join your on-call and walk through logs.

Sorry for the disruption; we want to be sure you have immediate relief and we'll follow up with a timeline and remediation summary.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
